> Nicotinamide mononucleotide (molecular formula: C11H15N2O8P, CAS number: 1094-61-7, also known as NMN, beta-Nicotinamide mononucleotide or β-NMN) is a vitamin B3 metabolite
>
> , naturally found in the human body, and in common foods such as broccoli and cabbage in tiny amounts[\[1\]]().[\[2\]]()  
NMN started to gain interest as a potential nutritional supplement in 2013, after a breakthrough study conducted by Harvard scientists on mice [\[3,4\]](https://www.plantpills.co.uk/nmn#references-and-further-reading).  
NMN was first produced as a supplement for humans in 2015 [\[5\]](https://www.plantpills.co.uk/nmn#references-and-further-reading), but was extremely expensive to manufacture, until methods were developed to reduce production costs and increase purity in 2018[\[6\]](https://www.plantpills.co.uk/nmn#references-and-further-reading), at which point laboratories geared up for mass production started to come online.
Notable further studies were conducted by Harvard scientists[\[7,8\]](https://www.plantpills.co.uk/nmn#references-and-further-reading).
Mice are not humans though, and promising results during trials on mice often do not transpire into positive results in humans. Multiple human trials are currently in progress [\[10,11,31\]](https://www.plantpills.co.uk/nmn#references-and-further-reading), with NMN appearing to be safe for humans to consume, and preliminary results are said to be promising[\[12\]](https://www.plantpills.co.uk/nmn#references-and-further-reading).  
> NMN is a precursor to the NAD+ molecule; the human body requires NMN in order to make its own NAD+.
>
> NAD+ is the oxidised form of NAD (Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide), a molecule first discovered in 1906, and found in all living cells.[\[13\]]()  
Supplementing with NAD+ itself is not an option to boost NAD+ levels, because it is too big to readily cross cell membranes to enter cells, and therefore would be unable to positively affect metabolism [\[23\]](https://www.plantpills.co.uk/nmn#references-and-further-reading).  
> We provide high purity, pharmaceutical grade, independently verified nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), for sale in the UK with delivery worldwide, at fair and reasonable prices for a material that is so expensive to produce.
>
> PlantPills NMN is manufactured using enzymatic synthesis (biosynthesis), as opposed to the cheaper chemical synthesis method which produces organic solvent residues that may be detrimental to health.
**Note:** A very detailed study into the SIRT1-LKB1-AMPK feedback loop in relation to [resveratrol](https://www.plantpills.co.uk/resveratrol), and the effect of resveratrol on various pathways concluded that using NMN (nicotinamide mononucleotide) to boost NAD levels will enable resveratrol to be effective[\[42\]](https://www.plantpills.co.uk/nmn#references-and-further-reading).
It can also be inferred that because of its indirect SIRT1 sirtuin activation, [resveratrol](https://www.plantpills.co.uk/resveratrol) may be needed to see the greatest effects from NMN.  
If you are taking prescription medication, consult your doctor before use.  
Keep contents in the packet or in a PlantPills Glass Jar until contents are finished. PlantPills Glass Jars that hold up to 20 grams of NMN are available for purchase in the shopping basket. These can provide a more convenient form of administering the daily servings while keeping the main packet stored away.  
Re-seal packet after use and store in a cool dry place. PlantPills NMN is stable at room temperature, but can be refrigerated. If room temperature exceeds 24 degrees Celsius, storing in a refrigerator is advisable. Avoid exposing NMN to moisture or high humidity.
